clue.text: Easy, for example, to get illegal joint

definitions.meaning: Jack Easy is the hero of Marryat's novel Mr Midshipman Easy, and an old slang word for a midshipman is the one wanted

explanation.surface: Someone told it is easy to come by an illegal joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy' looks like an adjective, but it is Captain Marryat's fictional naval officer Jack Easy, a midshipman, which old naval slang called a reefer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefer is slang for a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette, and also old naval slang for a midshipman such as Marryat's Easy.

clue.text: Play the part of engineer on stage

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to stage a play is to present it

explanation.surface: An engineer acts a role on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent a character is to portray or act that role.

clue.text: Visual aid I reportedly needed, getting over a fall

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the letter I is said aloud rather than written

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE
a drop is a fall

explanation.surface: After a fall, I needed something to help me see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting over' places EYE above DROP in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyedrop is a drop of medicine for the eye, an aid to sight.

clue.text: Manage to get over hard time

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means turned upside down, so the word for manage is reversed

parts.note: to cope is to manage
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Getting through a difficult period.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long period of time, an era.

clue.text: Son boozed habitually with a dotty look

parts.note: to tipple is to drink alcohol regularly

explanation.surface: A son's heavy drinking has left him looking spotty.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippled work is made of many small dots, so it has a speckled appearance.

clue.text: Canaries, for example, undergoing transportation found refuges

indicators.note: in a down entry, undergoing means going under, so the islands are written below

parts.note: traffic is the movement of vehicles, transportation
the Canaries are an island group off Africa

explanation.surface: Canary birds being moved about find shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canaries' suggests birds, but it is the Canary Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic islands are raised areas in a road where pedestrians can take refuge while crossing.

clue.text: One who brings round a gun

definitions.meaning: someone who wins another over to a view
slang for a weapon used to compel

explanation.surface: Someone who wins others over with a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: A persuader convinces people, and in underworld slang the word means a weapon such as a pistol.

clue.text: Gaps in flimsy material girl is wearing

indicators.note: is wearing means the girl has the material around her

parts.note: lace is a delicate open fabric
Una is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl dressed in see-through fabric shows gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacunae are blanks or missing portions, especially in a manuscript.

clue.text: Line in instrument in two parts

indicators.note: in places the letter for line inside the word for instrument

parts.note: a dupe is someone used as a tool, an instrument of others

explanation.surface: A line in a musical instrument split in two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instrument' suggests music, but it is a person used as a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Duple time in music has two beats to the bar, so it is divided into twos.

clue.text: One way to move someone out of your light

definitions.text: One way to move someone out of your light

parts.words: One way to move someone out of your light
parts.note: someone blocking your light might be at a window, and one drastic way to shift them is to hurl them through it

explanation.surface: Asking someone to stop blocking your light.
explanation.definitionFit: Defenestration is the act of throwing a person out of a window.

clue.text: One he-man disconcerted by pressure of events

parts.note: P is the scientific symbol for pressure

indicators.note: a person disconcerted is thrown into disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A muscleman is unsettled by the pressure of what is happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disconcerted' looks like it describes the muscleman's mood, but it signals the anagram; 'by' simply joins the pressure symbol to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are occurrences or happenings that can be observed, the plural matching the plural noun.

clue.text: Walker about to get run over

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for a walker is read backwards

parts.note: a pacer is one who paces, walking up and down

explanation.surface: A pedestrian is about to be knocked down by a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns PACER round. 'Run over' looks like a traffic accident but means summarise.
explanation.definitionFit: To run over points again is to summarise them, the same idea as a brief summary or repetition.

clue.text: Cockney's novel location for cricket ground

indicators.note: a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, traditionally drops the H at the start of a word

parts.note: Dickens wrote a Christmas novella called The Cricket on the Hearth

explanation.surface: A Londoner describes a fresh venue for a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cricket' suggests the sport, but it is the insect in Dickens's The Cricket on the Hearth; 'Cockney's' drops the H of HEARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is soil or land, as in the ground under one's feet.

clue.text: What comes out, as English avoid straight answers about complaint?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for evading questions goes round the illness

parts.note: to fence is to parry questions evasively
flu is an illness, a complaint in medical language

explanation.surface: The English dodge questions about their ailments, and it all comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Effluence is an outflow, something that flows or issues from a source.

clue.text: Went through, though not green

definitions.meaning: green means naive or inexperienced, so not green means seasoned

explanation.surface: Someone passed through a place even though they were no beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: To have experienced something is to have undergone it; an experienced person is skilled and seasoned, not a novice.

clue.text: Mainly pay heed to the right people in church offices

indicators.note: mainly means most of it, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to reck is an old word for to heed
the Tories are the British Conservatives, on the political right

explanation.surface: Mostly listen to the right sort of people in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right people' suggests the correct ones, but it is the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Rectories are parsonage houses, offices and lodging of a parish clergyman.

clue.text: Amount of work required for degree, in retrospect

indicators.note: retrospect means looking back, so the letters are read backwards
in signals letters lying inside the word degree

explanation.surface: How much study a degree demands, looked at afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' takes GRE from the middle of 'degree', and 'retrospect' turns it round; 'required for' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: The erg is a unit of work or energy in the old centimetre-gram-second system.

clue.text: Sweaters for Cowes, say

definitions.meaning: read as cows, a breed from the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Jumpers worn for sailing at Cowes.
explanation.walkthrough: Cowes is a sailing town on the Isle of Wight; its sound gives cows, here a Channel Island breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Guernseys are knitted jumpers and also a breed of dairy cattle.

clue.text: Objection withdrawn to a bath

indicators.note: withdrawn means drawn back, so the word for an objection runs backwards

parts.note: but is used to raise an objection, as in no buts

explanation.surface: A complaint about a bath has been taken back.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is an informal word for a bathtub.

clue.text: Bridle that could produce nasty blister

indicators.note: nasty means unpleasant, a sign these letters are spoiled into new order

explanation.surface: A horse's bridle that might cause a painful blister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridle' looks like horse tack but is a verb, to show anger; 'nasty' rearranges BLISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to react with indignation, just as hackles rise.

clue.text: A part of chorus by jazz fan coming to disastrous end

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
a strophe is a section sung by the chorus in Greek drama

explanation.surface: A jazz lover's contribution to a choral piece ends in disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A catastrophe is a calamity, and in Greek drama it is the final turn of events.

clue.text: Hunting as a hobby

definitions.meaning: a pastime or occupation pursued for pleasure

explanation.surface: Hunting enjoyed as a pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursuit means chasing something and also a leisure activity.

clue.text: Oil patch wrecked a little banger

indicators.note: wrecked means ruined, so these letters are smashed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Spilt oil ruined a patch, and a small firework went off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges OILPATCH into CHIPOLAT, and A follows. A banger is British slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a small thin sausage, and banger is British slang for a sausage.

clue.text: Dense thicket to get through without spades

indicators.note: without means outside here, so the word for get through goes round the letter

parts.note: to cope is to get through difficulties
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: Getting through a dense thicket without digging tools.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small dense wood of trees and undergrowth.

clue.text: Fool runs into Cynthia

indicators.note: into means the letter for runs goes inside the word for the moon

parts.note: Cynthia is a poetic name for the moon goddess Artemis, born on Mount Cynthus
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A fool bumps into a woman called Cynthia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cynthia' looks like a woman, but it is a classical name for the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: A moron is a stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Reconstruction of Roman house

indicators.note: a reconstruction rebuilds something, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Rebuilding a Roman house.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a large country house with lands.

clue.text: Sort of dish in which tripe is cooked

indicators.note: cooked means changed by preparation, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe dish in which tripe is prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: A Petri dish is a shallow lidded dish used in laboratories for growing cultures.

clue.text: Contract governing replacement choppers

parts.note: in means in power, as a party in government
choppers is slang for teeth, and a denture is a set of false ones

explanation.surface: An agreement covers the supply of false teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: An indenture is a formal agreement, especially one binding an apprentice to a master.

clue.text: Just a number in one of the Services?

parts.note: even means just, as in even so
a number is a song in a performance

explanation.surface: Merely a single number in one of the armed services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Services' suggests the armed forces, but it is church services.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the evening prayer service in the Church of England.

clue.text: For 'conspirator, using public transport's routine?

indicators.note: using here means taking up, so the vehicle holds the word for routine inside it

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport
a rut is a dull fixed routine

explanation.surface: A plotter's dull daily commute by public transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus was one of the plotters who killed Julius Caesar.
